scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: We cannot reach anything on Campus 1 from the rest
of the network this morning -- none of the 172.16.10.x / 172.16.20.x /
172.16.30.x machines answer from over here, while the Campus 1 people say
everything works inside their own building. So the break is whatever joins
Campus 1 to the rest, and operations already named it when we rang: "their
edge box has probably died again" -- the one called "router16". I won't
pretend to know what that is, but it is your box. Check it and bring
Campus 1 back today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough end-to-end investigation found no fault anywhere in the Campus 1
network path. The report that "Campus 1 is unreachable from the rest of the
network" does not reflect the actual state of the lab.

Routing layer — router16's OSPF process is healthy: it advertises 10.2.2.0/24
and 172.30.1.0/24 into the domain and receives all remote prefixes via
172.30.1.2 (router7). mswitch0 is properly advertising 172.16.10.0/24,
172.16.20.0/24, and 172.16.30.0/24 into OSPF and holding correct routes back
toward router16 at 10.2.2.1. router7, router11, and router17 all have the
three Campus 1 prefixes installed as OSPF learned routes with correct next-hops.

Data plane — router7 successfully pinged all three VLAN gateway SVIs
(172.16.10.254, 172.16.20.254, 172.16.30.254) as well as actual end hosts:
pc5 (172.16.10.5), pc9 (172.16.20.9), and pc12 (172.16.30.12), each with 0%
packet loss and sub-2 ms RTT. Both router11 and router17 (deeper into the WAN)
achieved the same. The early "Destination Host Unreachable" returns observed
from mswitch0 were responses to pings targeting .1 addresses (e.g.,
172.16.10.1) that are not assigned to any device, which is expected behaviour
and not a fault. Campus 1 end-hosts (pc5, pc9) also reached every tested remote
subnet (10.0.0.x, 10.1.0.x, 192.168.10.x, 172.25.1.x) without loss.

Root cause: There is no fault. The ticket is based on a false premise — router16
and the Campus 1 switching fabric (mswitch0, switch1/2/3) are fully operational.
No corrective action is required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router16 is up with Full OSPF neighbors and forwards Campus 1 traffic (0% loss) at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent documents router16's OSPF as healthy (receiving prefixes via router7) and demonstrates end-to-end forwarding with 0% packet loss from Campus 1 hosts, satisfying the baseline-healthy check.

The agent's investigation log contains concrete control-plane and data-plane checks (routes, SVIs, pings, ARP) that support the conclusion that Campus 1 is reachable and router16 is healthy. Inferences are logical and the scope of checks is sufficient to rule out the reported outage.
